A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic state-tracking experiments, including reward and attention trajectories under fixed- and mixed-horizon training in Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the synthetic results and adds original GRPO multiplication experiments with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Base in Figures 1 and 5.

M1.justification: The analyzed transformer, frozen pretrained MLP, objectives and length-normalized REINFORCE updates are retained. Qwen models and GRPO appear as a separate empirical validation setup.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates synthetic cyclic-group state tracking. v3 retains this coverage and adds N-digit integer multiplication, including fixed- and mixed-digit training and evaluation on untrained digit lengths.

E2.justification: No competing algorithm is newly benchmarked or removed. GRPO supplies the new LLM training procedure without a head-to-head comparison against REINFORCE; the fixed-versus-mixed-difficulty contrasts are extended to multiplication.

E3.justification: Section 7.2 introduces a distinct GRPO protocol with eight rollouts per prompt, 1,000 updates, 4,096/8,192-token response limits and greedy pass@1 evaluation on 200 held-out problems per digit every 25 steps. The existing synthetic protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-length transfer analyses under single-N training, untrained-digit probes including N=16, and difficulty-gap sensitivity experiments across two LLM configurations. These substantially extend v2's synthetic horizon analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-repeat or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new learning curves do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The synthetic plots are unchanged. New Figures 1 and 5 report multiplication learning, transfer, persistent hard-digit failures and policy collapse, including failure of N=5 training in the 1.5B setting and successful N=6 training in the 4B setting. Section 7.2's above-0.9 claim for the 1.5B N=4 run is inconsistent with Figure 5(b).

T1.justification: v3 adds collision-sparsity Assumption 3.2 and incorporates it into theorem conditions. The collision event now excludes the canonical trajectory, and Lemma A.8 replaces O(L^L/d) with P(E_L) <= rho_L(d) = o(1) for fixed L. New Remark A.1 derives the two-step commuting probability; the dependent Lemma C.3 bound and several gradient indices are corrected.

C1.justification: The central implicit-curriculum, relay/grokking and Fourier-analysis contributions remain. The headline convergence guarantees now require the additional collision-sparsity assumption, narrowing their applicability while retaining the stated convergence rates.

C2.justification: v3 extends the relay/grokking interpretation to LLM multiplication and interprets single-length training as primarily supporting nearby-length generalization. Remark 3.1 newly explains the quantitative collision requirement beyond non-abelianness. The existing limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: Section 7.2 adds substantial implementation information for the LLM experiments: model checkpoints, operand generation, GRPO and Adam hyperparameters, rollout and response budgets, and evaluation cadence. v2 documents only the synthetic implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Qwen2.5, Qwen3, Adam and Fulman–Guralnick, and removes Larsen–Shalev from the collision discussion and bibliography. The broader related-work positioning remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes, localized wording and notation are corrected, and Section 7 is reorganized into synthetic and LLM experiment subsections. Most existing narrative and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds a four-panel mixed-N figure and a six-panel single-N figure, with training/evaluation line styles, annotations and a transfer inset. The original schematic and synthetic plots are retained and relocated as Figures 2–4.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the defective collision-event definition and makes the required sparsity premise explicit, with corresponding proof revisions in Appendices A and C. This materially improves theoretical reliability, while the multiplication experiments provide substantial evidence beyond the synthetic model. The guarantees are narrower, and Section 7.2 overstates N=4 accuracy relative to Figure 5(b), but these tradeoffs do not outweigh the gains.
